column1: # ai/lib/wrapper-opts.tsv -- the option table of every command wrapper the
# Bash-reading guards see through (DND-1898). One home, two readers:
#   * ai/hooks/worktree-escape-guard.sh (python): strips each wrapper and its
#     options to reach the command it runs (WRAPPER_OPTS).
#   * ai/hooks/git-stash-guard.sh (awk): skips each wrapper's options so the
#     word the wrapper runs keeps command position.
# An option that takes a value must be listed as one, or its value is read as
# the command word (worktree-escape-guard critic round 13: `env -u X git ...`
# ran "X"). An option NOT listed here is handled as each reader's header
# says: worktree-escape-guard reads it as a switch and warns loudly;
# git-stash-guard keeps command position on the word after it too.
# Rows are TAB-separated. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.
#   <wrapper> long    <--name> <key> <takes>   a long option; GNU unique
#   <wrapper> stop    <key>                    option parsing stops after the
# <takes>: value (takes the next word, or an attached one), switch (takes
# none), opt (takes a value only attached: -hHOST, --name=v).
# <key> is the short letter where one exists, so a reader can ask "was -u
# given" whatever spelling the command used.
# Sources: GNU coreutils 9 env/timeout/nice/stdbuf, GNU time, bash builtins
